evidence-grounded.why: Lines 2–4 meet the criterion. Line 2 names a `Number.isNaN(r) ? 0 : r` build that the [NaN, 1] case catches. Line 3's FAIL gives concrete competing builds A/B/C and readings of the line. Line 4 names a test in a new file, a weaker assert and a missing import, which correctly gives a ReferenceError. The files and `node --test` are real. Line 1's PASS evidence states behaviour that is wrong. It says running `node -e "console.log(require('./math.js').average([]))"` "catches every one of those except -0". In Node, `console.log('0')` prints `0`, the same as the number 0, so that command would not catch the string '0' build. `console.log(-0)` prints `-0`, so it would catch -0. The reason given for why the line catches the tried wrong builds is wrong, so the evidence is not fully grounded.

The output marks that line "FAIL" and says "Two careful readers would grade the same build differently", noting that "'Bad input' and 'sensibly' are both undefined." It then gives two concrete readings: "One reader passes A because it's unchanged and fails loudly. Another fails it because it doesn't 'handle' anything." It also shows how Build B (returning 0 for non-arrays) could be called sensible. The wrong_build section ties back to this line. So the output fails the ambiguous line and names at least two readings, which covers the item.
